outlook: Grains were mostly a little higher overnight after Wednesday's mixed close, with analysts calling corn, soybeans and wheat oversold. On Wednesday December corn hit new lows early but reversed to close up 1¼ cents at $4.63¼, ending a six-day losing streak, while November soybeans fell for an eighth straight session to $12.45¼ despite sales to China and Spain. Wheat dropped sharply on talk of a Ukraine peace deal and possible U.S.-Russia-China talks: December Chicago lost 15 cents to $6.28¼ and Minneapolis December spring wheat lost 10¼ cents to $6.51½. Crude oil rallied toward $100 a barrel on Middle East tensions overnight, and rain in the Upper Midwest this weekend could slow harvest.
